decision: Should Phase 4 add a bounded rural/satellite decision shape to the live broadband lens, and can that pilot be built without crossing an inherited release gate?
liveConsumer: A rural or constrained U.S. household using the published broadband guide and Broadband & internet explorer to compare the providers actually available at its address.

gates.evidence: The founder directed Codex to begin Phase 4 on 2026-07-15.
The published broadband guide explicitly tells users with constrained choices to compare cable, DSL, fixed wireless, or satellite, but the live 12-entry lens contains no satellite option.

sourceRequirements: FCC National Broadband Map and Broadband Consumer Label rules for technology, availability, pricing, and disclosure boundaries.
Current first-party Starlink service-plan, fair-use, privacy, and terms pages.
Current first-party Hughesnet plan, broadband-label, priority-data, privacy, and subscriber terms.
Current first-party Viasat plan, broadband-label, network-management, privacy, and subscriber terms.

preconditions.evidence: The broadband lens has 12 U.S. options across fiber, cable, and fixed wireless; satellite entries = 0 while the guide names satellite as a real constrained-household route.
This capsule owns only audit and review artifacts. Phase 2 remains ledger-blocked, so the broadband lens and generated outputs are forbidden until the dataset build path is reconciled.

doneWhen: A reproducible audit distinguishes earned decision-shape demand from category count growth.
A three-option candidate matrix names the exact primary evidence needed for all five existing broadband criteria.
The prior Phase 2 ledger state is checked before any dataset-backed content write.
No lens, pipeline, generated app, or design-owned file is edited while the build gate is closed.
A terminal result records whether the pilot is executable or blocked and the smallest safe follow-up.
stopConditions: The pilot would add providers merely to increase roster size rather than represent a missing access technology.
Current address-level plan evidence cannot support the five existing criteria without inventing universal prices or availability.
Any content edit would require running the Phase 2-modified dataset generator against unresolved provenance verification.
The work would hand-edit generated app data or cross into search/UX code.
expectedArtifacts: A frozen rural-broadband evidence and candidate baseline.
A terminal result card with the exact build gate and follow-up.

claimBoundary.supports: The live broadband decision has a bounded missing satellite route and three current primary-source candidates can be prepared without editing data.
claimBoundary.doesNotSupport: That satellite is preferable to terrestrial broadband, universally available, uniformly priced, or safe to add before the dataset build gate is green.
